name: Meter flow without a valid deal: extension, new-deal and write-off requests
description: Volume management, logistics and settlement staff find gas flowing at an HPL meter with no active Sitara deal. The deal may have expired or missed its evergreen roll, the flow may be parked on the Strangers Gas contract, or the meter may be new. They email Daren Farmer, one meter at a time, asking him to extend or roll a deal, create a new one, or sign a printed write-off to Unaccounted for Gas. Allocation, accounting arrangements and invoicing cannot go ahead until he answers. This is the largest and most frequent process in the archive. Nearly every batch shows it, and almost all of it runs through one person.
stall_points: Every request waits on Daren Farmer, who is also trading, so requesters send reminders and the same meters come back the next month. Write-offs need a printed, signed and returned original. Forwarded threads carry long quoted history. Feedback and bridge errors pass through four or five people before reaching the deal owner. Deal numbers are sometimes wrong or sit with another desk, and suspended counterparties or expired contracts block the fix.
automation: A daily and month-end exception job that compares allocated meter flow with active Sitara deals and lists every meter with flow and no deal, including Strangers Gas allocations and lapsed evergreens. Each exception goes to the deal owner as a pre-filled work item with the meter, days, volume and the prior deal proposed for extension, plus one-click options to extend, create or approve a write-off electronically, with status tracking and automatic reminders. This replaces the one-off emails, the printed approval forms and the chasers.
